eps.d: George and Mildred Roper plan a move to middle class suburbia. Mildred is anxious to impress, but George is happy to remain working class.
The Ropers meet the new neighbours and their invisible dog, and George discusses politics with the local MP.
The Ropers have moved, so George must find a job.
Mildred becomes broody and starts to dream of motherhood - much to George's dismay.
When Mildred finds out that George only has a small endowment, she decides to do something about it.
George buys a caravan but is towed away while asleep in it.
George begins to resent the fact that Mildred treats the dog better than she does him.
The Ropers discover that the local pub serves draught gin and tonic, and George accuses his next-door neighbour of attempted murder.
Mildred becomes a TV widow when the Ropers's ancient set breaks down.

Mildred's mother visits, but the family believe that she is too old to look after herself and decide to place her in a home. However, George unexpectedly takes Mildred's mother's side and asks her to stay with them.
Mildred inadvertently contributes George's stash of gardening books to a church, but learns that they were actually old pornographic magazines, and must retrieve them before the vicar finds out!
George buys Mildred a carriage clock for her birthday, but later learns the Fourmiles had been robbed and the clock might have once belonged to them.
When Mildred rents out the backroom to a travelling salesman, George begins to believe the two are having an affair!
Mildred's sister Ethel and her husband Humphrey are coming round for a meal but George has forgotten to pay the electricity bill.
Mildred wants socialist George to join the local Tory party so they can qualify for a cheap holiday, courtesy of the Conservative Association.
While cleaning, Mildred finds an old case containing George's old love letters written to someone named 'Dorothy'...
The Fourmiles host a Christmas pantomime but are short an 'ugly sister', so Mildred is asked to stand in.
Jerry manages to trick George into trying to sell the house behind Mildred's back.
The Ropers' bed finally collapses after 25 years, so Mildred decides to buy a new one... but George thinks that the nearest bookmaker is the best chance of getting the money.
Mildred receives a letter requesting a meeting, from an American former airman, with whom she had a wartime fling...
George is forced to look for a job.
Ann finally gives birth, so George and Mildred help her out.
George's father is kicked out of his retirement home and asks to live with the Ropers.
George manages to get a job as a traffic warden.
Whilst drinking in the pub, George runs into a man who claims to be his long lost son.
Mildred decides to have a new shower installed in the bathroom. After several quotes, Jerry gets the job.
George quits his job but cannot bring himself to inform Mildred.
Mildred is out at a pottery class, leaving George stuck with the Fourmiles' baby. But while looking after him, George gets a call to join the pub's darts team.
Mildred wants the dog to have puppies but George sees it as an opportunity to get some extra cash.

eps.t: On the Second Day of Christmas
eps.d: The Ropers are having another boring Christmas, so the Fourmiles invite them over for a drink. George then challenges Tristram to a game of computer tennis and wins. Afterwards, George plays Jeffrey, but ends up losing sixteen times... and owing a hefty debt!
It's the Ropers' wedding anniversary and George has bought Mildred an expensive looking coat When she asks him where the money came from she discovers that he has found somebody's credit card.
With Mildred in hospital, a lonely George has Jerry move in with him.
Mildred is unhappy at her lack of social success, so she thinks about moving to Australia.
Mildred is flattered when George displays a rare stirring of jealousy, following a sighting of her in a car with another man.
George's brother Charlie turns up with an interesting document.
When Mildred flushes George's goldfish down the drain, he decides that he needs a new pet.
Mildred notices a photo of an expensive antique in a magazine. Coincidentally, it looks just like one she has hidden away upstairs.
Mildred decides she wants to go to the Tory Christmas ball, but George has other plans.
